name: Insiders

subjectOf.text: Under the fairness to the public definition, a fair token launch requires that the token was launched without a founding team, a foundation, or a founding dev team.
subjectOf.abstract: Under this definition, a fair token launch requires that the token was launched without a founding team, foundation, or founding dev team.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: strict fairness to the public definition of fair launch

subjectOf.text: The rule that no tokens may be distributed to insiders such as team, founders, associated whales, core investors, advisors, and marketing teams before or after the token sale is the most important staple of fair launch doctrine and cannot be subject to exceptions; any exception should cost the project the fair token launch designation.
subjectOf.abstract: This rule is perhaps the most important key staple of the fair launch doctrine and cannot be subject to exceptions. Any exceptions to this rule should result in the loss of the designation fair token launch.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: projects claiming the fair token launch designation

subjectOf.text: Community DAO governance makes any form of rug pull much less likely, because rug pulls typically benefit only a few select individuals who retained control over the project code or liquidity.
subjectOf.abstract: Community DAO governance also makes any form of rug pulls much less likely as rug pulls typically only benefit a few select individuals who retained control over the project code or liquidity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Fair Token Launch (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4015908
scope_conditions: community DAO oversees project code and liquidity
